body_markdown:
Why do so many businesses struggle to turn data into faster decisions? Neil Bunn, Director of Customer Engineering, Strategic Verticals Canada at Google Cloud, shares his take with Technology Strategist, Lisa Martin in this OpenStudio conversation. His answer: pair AI agents that can dig through massive amounts of data with the trusted information OpenText helps organizations manage, and put governance and security around it. The payoff is clearer insight, quicker responses when markets shift, and more confidence in the decisions you make.


## **Watch the Full Interview:**


OpenStudio: Turning Trusted Data into Faster Decisions with Google Cloud – Featuring Neil Bunn


## **Three Key Takeaways**


- **Let AI agents do the digging.** Neil Bunn describes agents as tireless explorers that can sift through huge volumes of data and uncover correlations people might never get to.


- **Pair cloud power with business know-how.** Google has spent 25 years working with unstructured data at web scale, and OpenText brings deep experience as a trusted custodian of critical business information. Together, that’s a strong combination.


- **Move fast without losing control.** Neil Bunn ties quicker responses to changing conditions back to trust, governance, security and giving agents access in a controlled way.


## **Why is it so difficult to unlock value from enterprise data?**


Here’s the thing, according to Neil Bunn: this isn’t a new problem, but it’s a much bigger one now. Teams have been gathering data since the early days of simple databases, yet today’s sheer volume makes deep exploration tough for people to tackle alone. The real question is how to find useful connections without letting manual investigation become the bottleneck.


“But that’s exactly where agentic workflows and agents come into play,” says Neil Bunn. “They have the ultimate patience for sitting and exploring data and the ultimate ability to sit and create correlations and derive value from data.”


Think of agents as the teammate with endless patience: they can keep exploring large datasets and surface correlations that people may not have time to chase.


## **What does the OpenText–Google Cloud partnership add?**


Bunn sees two strengths that fit nicely together. Google built technologies to gather and work with unstructured information on the web, and OpenText brings experience safeguarding information that matters to business operations. Pairing that technical foundation with business expertise is the point, because cloud infrastructure alone isn’t the whole answer.


Neil Bunn describes OpenText as “a trusted custodian for large volumes of really critical business data.” He sums up the shared ambition this way: “Make these things useful, valuable and accessible.”


Bunn’s comparison is clear: Google brings experience gathering unstructured data at web scale, while OpenText brings trusted custody of critical business information. Together, he says, they can unlock value. For more, explore[OpenText’s Google Cloud partnership and solution resources](https://www.opentext.com/partners/opentext-on-google-cloud) .


## **Where could faster insight change a business outcome?**


Bunn’s answer comes down to decision velocity. Picture a supply chain thrown off by weather or geopolitical change: the value is in understanding what happened and pivoting sooner.


“Providing better data into decision making frameworks that allow a business to react to an event quicker or to pivot when market conditions change quicker,” says Neil Bunn.


So, the question isn’t just “What can we learn from our data?” It’s “Which decision would that insight help us make sooner?” Bunn points to moving faster, more accurately and with better underlying intelligence as where the business value shows up.


## **How can organizations give agents access without giving up control?**


Bunn lays out a practical path: understand your business processes, build trust and governance in early, wrap your data in a security layer, and then give agents controlled access to explore. Speed and control work hand in hand.


“You have to think through your processes,” says Neil Bunn, who adds that organizations should “focus on that trust layer really early on.”


In practice, that means wrapping data in a security layer and giving agents access “in a controlled fashion” so they can mine valuable insight quickly.


## **Explore the evidence and related reading**


- **Research:**[The State of AI Security & Governance: 2025 Report](https://cloud.google.com/resources/content/csa-the-state-of-ai-security-and-governance) , from CSA and Google Cloud Security, provides further context on governance and enterprise AI readiness.


- **Customer evidence:**[OpenText’s Experience Cloud customer story](https://www.opentext.com/customers/opentext-experience-cloud) describes OpenText’s own digital-experience transformation using Experience Cloud and Google Cloud Platform. This is a separate, published example—not a customer outcome claimed in this interview.


- **Related post:**[From Sovereign Cloud to Agentic AI](https://blogs.opentext.com/from-sovereign-cloud-to-agentic-ai/) explores the OpenText–Google Cloud partnership through governed information, sovereignty and OpenText™ Content Aviator.

## **Full Interview Transcript**


*The full interview transcript is reproduced below without changes.*


## **Introduction**


**Lisa Martin:** Did you know that some of the world’s largest enterprises are still struggling to really capture value from vast amounts of data? Well, when you enter the powerful partnership of OpenText with Google Cloud, that is where things get so much simpler because what they’re doing is they’re combining trusted governed information with scalable cloud infrastructure plus AI. They’re helping clients like you accelerate innovation and deliver what you want, real business outcomes. I’m Lisa Martin, and I’m really happy to be joined by Neil Bunn. Neil is the Director of Customer Engineering, Strategic Verticals Canada at Google Cloud.


## **Current Challenges**


**Lisa Martin:** Talk to me about some of the challenges organizations are facing to unlock value from so much data.


**Neil Bunn:** Yeah, I mean, it’s such an expansive problem, and it’s not a new one. I mean, like from time beginning in computing, everybody knew we can gather some data and we’ll try to find some value in it. In the earliest days, that was simply just simple databases. But at this point, sheer volumes of data makes it very difficult for people to kind of explore and unlock really deep insights from that data is just beyond what most people can imagine. But that’s exactly where agentic workflows and agents come into play. They have the ultimate patience for sitting and exploring data and the ultimate ability to sit and create correlations and derive value from data.


## **The Partnership**


**Lisa Martin:** Walk me through a little bit in terms of the power of the partnership. Google Cloud, OpenText, You’re combining your technologies. We’re talking about engineering expertise. How are you doing that together to help clients overcome that challenge that you just mentioned?


**Neil Bunn:** Right. What you kind of have to remember that Google ourselves, like we started with a very consumer oriented problem like organizing the world’s data, making it universally accessible, but mostly in a web context. And we built a whole series of technologies to be able to consume and gather unstructured data, at mass. And we’ve been doing that for 25 years for the web. But where Open Text comes into play is like the legacy of being so strong in being a trusted custodian for large volumes of really critical business data. Now, if you layer our technologies underneath that, with the domain expertise and the innovation that OpenText can bring to the fore, we can really actually start to unlock values. And I think that’s really interesting because it fits our shared mission, vision and mandate, right? Make these things useful, valuable and accessible.


## **Business Outcomes**


**Lisa Martin:** What are some of the key business outcomes? Because it’s all about what am I doing that’s really delivering value to my business that you guys can together help clients enable.


**Neil Bunn:** For us, A lot of it is actually about increasing decision velocity, right? Providing better data into decision making frameworks that allow a business to react to an event quicker or to pivot when market conditions change quicker. You know, there’s several of these classic supply chain challenges of like whether it’s weather oriented or geopolitical, whatever changes. Being able to kind of very quickly pivot drives tremendous value. And that’s actually how most clients get ahead of each other, right? There’s a lot of really base understanding to businesses these days, but where you excel a business is if you can move faster, more accurately and with better underlying intelligence. And the two of us come together that way very, very strongly. You have to think through your processes. You have to, to your point, like focus on that trust layer really early on and trust in governance. That requires some very sophisticated understanding of business processes. And it’s something OpenText has always been extraordinarily strong in. And the governance layer and the technologies to enforce that are a number of things that are the strength of Google Cloud. And so when you kind of combine those two things together, you can rapidly innovate like we have for several clients with really innovative ways of kind of taking that data, wrapping the security layer around it, giving a pile of agents access in a controlled fashion and allowing it to mine out that super valuable insight very, very quickly. Being able to do those things together has been fantastic.


## **Wrap Up**


**Lisa Martin:** Oh, it’s a mic drop moment. Neil, thank you so much for stopping by and sharing really very symbiotically the power of Google Cloud and OpenText. Appreciate your time.


**Neil Bunn:** The partnership is fantastic and we really appreciate it. Thank you.


**Lisa Martin:** We want to thank you for watching. For Neil Bunn I’m Lisa Martin. We’ll see you next time.
